title: Imperial charter-and-guild culture
scope: Qualitative charter-and-guild organizing logic of the withdrawn imperial power — chartered-body government, corporate personhood, virtue and sin field, faith orientation class, livery dress pattern, and ecological-suppression value — together with its drifted living remnant expression at the outlet settlement; usable for culture, attitude, and remnant-texture development without establishing names, languages, script or vocabulary, rite content, monetary facts, dates, measurements, demography, outlet-settlement government or institutions, or any change to natural System behaviour.
claims: The withdrawn power governed as a lattice of chartered bodies — guilds, colleges, companies, temple-corporations — each holding delegated authority under written charter; membership was identity, and law was charter interpretation argued between bodies.
Full personhood in practice was corporate: standing ran through one's body, and the unincorporated held thin standing.

Absorbed peoples were incorporated as recognized native bodies under limited charters or joined imperial bodies as junior members, and ambitious original-culture families earned or bought membership; how the region came under the power is not established here.

Internal variation existed, at minimum between the metropole's dense overlapping charters and the frontier's reliance on one or two bodies holding sweeping local grants — a works company, a garrison college.

Its virtue set — fidelity to charter, craft excellence, mutual aid within the body, and honest accounting between bodies — was genuinely admirable in part, for charters restrained arbitrary power and gave the low-born collective standing no lone petitioner had; its sin set — charter-breach, encroachment on another body's chartered work, betrayal of craft secrets, and letting a chartered work fail — condemned real harms, and the same fidelity that protected members froze out the unincorporated; neither list renders the culture simply good or evil.
Its faith orientation was a charter-granting cult class: the divine imagined as ultimate issuer of warrants, with each body keeping licensed observance of its patron-craft cult; belief only.
Dress followed livery: body-membership livery classes and craft-mark classes, with grade shown in trim and a forbidden-marks class covering other bodies' livery and revoked charters' marks.

Its ecological-suppression ideology held that the wild was unchartered ground — land became grantable, ownable, and real only once a charter covered it — and suppression was contracted out to clearance-companies as profitable duty; this is value, not an added collapse cause.

At the outlet settlement, membership-identity persists strongly — belonging to a working body is who you are — with craft-mark pride and the habit of writing agreements down and appealing to old grants; charter authority has hollowed because the granting centre is gone, so partial, disputed, possibly forged documents carry weight with no court able to renew or adjudicate them; the delegation has inverted, so bodies that were branches of a lattice now behave as sovereigns of their own function; and the drift is contested, with younger outlet generations treating charter-piety as elders' habit and quiet operators simply working outside the old marks.

The imperial-descended households admitted into the ridge-spur settlement in its early days came out of this culture; that admission, its terms, and its consequences belong to canon://world/shared-universe-001/culture/settlement-founding-fusion-blend and are neither duplicated nor extended here.

The imperial culture was literate, standardizing, and engineering-minded, consistent with the accepted remnant records, and it administered the original culture's region for generations as a peripheral holding of a power centred elsewhere.

The outlet settlement is the imperial culture's primary living local continuation — carried by imperial-descended people through the withdrawal and later gathered at the reused nucleus, which was abandoned before it was re-occupied; two clocks run separately, drift from the metropole may begin at centre failure while post-authority remnant drift at the outlet begins only when organised imperial presence ended regionally, neither that span nor the re-occupation is dated here, and the result is improvised, internally varied, and contested — never frozen, uniform, or fanatical by default.
Internal variation existed historically, at minimum between metropole and frontier expressions, and persists in the remnant.

The imperial culture also changed across its own history: each recovery-and-fall cycle stripped further function layers and stranded frontier offices decayed in place at different rates, so the form this region experienced in the arc's later phases was already stripped and improvised relative to its metropole ideal, and the remnant inherited a late degraded form, not the full system; no cycle count, date, or stripped-function inventory is added.
All faith content in this record is belief and orientation class only; no cosmology, rite content, or afterlife claim is confirmed.

All imperial and remnant use of System records is cultural practice — access, interpretation, presentation — over unchanged natural System behaviour, with no guaranteed readout, no System-executed office, and no institution owning any person's progression.
No imperial work, record, or institution survives functioning as designed; remnant recognition is cultural recognition, not accurate knowledge of function.
Remnant beliefs about the empire, its fall, and its works are attitude and memory, not evidence of what actually occurred.
boundaries: This record is a forward culture extension filling WLD-HISTORY-001's and WLD-LOCATION-005's declared-open imperial-culture space; it moves no accepted claim, and every open boundary of every record it touches stays open except through the two declared closures stated here.

Charter, body, guild, college, company, temple-corporation, grant, warrant, livery, craft mark, trim grade, forbidden-marks class, charter-granting cult, and clearance-company are author-facing qualitative descriptions fixing no in-world name, language, title text, charter or code wording, body count, office count, calendar, measurement, proportion, price, or performance guarantee; imperial is author-facing shorthand for the withdrawn power.

Declared qualitative closure of WLD-HISTORY-001's open imperial-culture space: the withdrawn power's qualitative organizing logic — formal structure, personhood logic, virtue and sin field, faith orientation class, dress pattern, and ecological-suppression value — is closed to the charter-and-guild frame; within that record's separately open question of what the organised ecological suppression consisted of, this closure reaches one narrow element only — the contracting class named in claim 8, clearance let out under charter to companies — and the methods, scale, costs, institutions beyond that contracting class, and everything else WLD-HISTORY-001 leaves open about what that suppression consisted of stay open; its name, capital, heartland, language, extent, formal offices and their counts, rulers, generals, officials, cycle counts, dates, and map relation beyond peripheral status all remain open, as does the region's route of incorporation.

Declared qualitative closure of WLD-LOCATION-005's open cultural texture: the outlet settlement's primarily-imperial character receives this record's qualitative drift pattern — what persists, what hollows, what inverts — and nothing further; that settlement's name, founding date, the nucleus's re-occupation date and reuse history, size, population, government, leadership, institutions, law, defences, economy, internal composition, and minority presence all remain open, and primarily still does not mean uniformly.

The drift span is unfixed: WLD-HISTORY-001 fixes no regional end date for organised imperial presence, this record fixes none, and neither the outlet settlement's founding date nor the nucleus's re-occupation date is established.

The suppression ideology is a value, never a cause; no collapse cause, phase, weighting, trigger, date, or event is added, WLD-HISTORY-001's multi-causal frame with its open trigger stands, and no legitimacy-erosion or other structural collapse driver is established.

WLD-LOCATION-004 continues to establish that no remnant functions as designed; the remnant documents here are explicitly partial, disputed, and possibly forged, no intact archive, verified grant, functioning mechanism, or working imperial machinery exists, no exception is created, and that record's claim 3 sequence is preserved rather than overridden — no imperial work is continuously occupied since its abandonment, so this culture is carried by people rather than by unbroken occupation of the nucleus, the abandonment-then-re-occupation order stands, and each work's local abandonment timing and the nucleus's reuse history stay open.
No closure is declared of WLD-LOCATION-004's open remnant-attitude space: cultural recognition of remnants stays recognition, not knowledge of function, and avoidance remains practical, not ritual.

The company-country texture of the frontier resonates with the industrial village nucleus WLD-LOCATION-005 records but assigns that nucleus no imperial-era function, which stays open per WLD-LOCATION-005.

The remnant is internally varied and contested, never uniform or fanatical by default; no outlet faction, leader, government, institution, law, membership roster, surviving body, or occurred dispute is established.

WLD-CULTURE-001's ex-imperial functionary or garrison descendant strand gains historical depth only; that record's lived attitude spectrum toward the imperial inheritance is untouched, no strand gains unanimity or exclusive System truth, and no strand, household, or lineage is assigned a body, membership, livery, or craft mark.

WLD-CULTURE-002 is untouched: this record's charter is the withdrawn power's corporate instrument class and fixes nothing about the ridge-spur founder charter-oath compact, its structure, its offices, or its designed ambiguities, and no governance claim is made for either settlement.

The imperial-descended households admitted into the ridge-spur settlement came out of this culture and nothing more about that admission is established here; its terms, its consequences, the settlement's relations between cultures, and the state of any blending there belong solely to canon://world/shared-universe-001/culture/settlement-founding-fusion-blend, and this record establishes nothing about the ridge-spur settlement's internal cultural relations.

The original culture appears here only as a structural position — incorporated as recognized native bodies under limited charters or as junior members of imperial bodies; its internal frame, content, and lived experience under administration belong to canon://world/shared-universe-001/culture/original-kin-hall-season-court-culture.
